mainTopic: Witnesses who saw separately (עדות מיוחדת), who must give the התראה, and hearing testimony through an interpreter
overview: The משנה teaches that two pairs of witnesses at two windows count as one testimony only if some of them can see each other. Otherwise they are two testimonies, so if one pair turns out to be עדים זוממין, the accused and that pair are executed while the other pair goes free. רבי יוסי adds that the witnesses themselves must give the התראה, and that the סנהדרין may not hear testimony through an interpreter. The גמרא learns from 'לא יומת על פי עד אחד' that עדות מיוחדת is invalid. It adds that even witnesses at one window who watched one after the other do not join, and אביי explains that this teaching is needed for the case of forbidden relations. רבא rules that the witnesses join if they see the מתרה or he sees them, and that the warning can come from anyone. רב נחמן says עדות מיוחדת is valid in money cases, but רב זוטרא raises a difficulty from the משנה that remains a קשיא. Finally, the גמרא shows that the רבי יוסי who does not require התראה for a שונא is really רבי יוסי בר יהודה. It also explains that רבא could use an interpreter because he understood the witnesses himself and needed help only to answer them.

steps.title: Witnesses at two windows: one testimony or two?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes two pairs of witnesses at two windows with one warner in the middle. If some of them see each other, it is one testimony. If not, it is two testimonies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two people watched him from one window and two from another, and one person in the middle warned him. If some of the witnesses can see each other, they are one testimony. If not, they are two separate testimonies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a case of four witnesses split between two windows and rules on whether they form one group or two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is whether the witnesses can see one another. If at least some can, the two pairs merge into one big עדות. If none can, each pair stands alone as its own separate עדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives a warning (התראה) before the sin, which is required for punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Not every witness has to see every other one. The משנה says 'some of them' (מקצתן), so it is enough that some of the witnesses see each other.

phrases.english: MISHNAH

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ, מֵחַלּוֹן זֶה,
phrases.english: If there were two seeing him from this window,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is a person doing a sin that carries the death penalty.

phrases.english: and two seeing him from that window,
and one warning him in the middle,

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן רוֹאִין אֵלּוּ אֶת אֵלּוּ –
phrases.english: when some of them see each other,
they are one testimony;
and if not,
they are two testimonies.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ, מֵחַלּוֹן זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses at separate windows join into one testimony only if some of them see each other; otherwise they are two testimonies.

steps.title: Result when one of the two sets is found lying
steps.stepSummary: Because they are two separate testimonies, if one pair is proven זוממין, the accused (convicted by the other pair) and the lying pair are both executed, and the second pair is free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, if one of the sets is found to be זוממין, he and they are executed, and the second set is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a practical result from the 'two testimonies' ruling: what happens when one pair is caught lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each pair is its own עדות, disproving one pair does not cancel the other. The valid pair still convicts the accused, and the lying pair gets the punishment of עדים זוממין, which is death. If they were one testimony, the whole thing would fall together.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore: a result that follows from the ruling before it
A set of עדים זוממין, witnesses proven to have lied because they were elsewhere at the time

steps.confusionAlert: 'He' (הוא) is the accused, who is executed because of the valid second set. 'They' (הן) are the lying set. The second set did nothing wrong, so it is פטורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the 'one testimony or two' question matters in practice. It decides whether a disproven pair brings down the whole case.

phrases.english: Therefore, if there is found
one of them to be conspiring witnesses,
he and they are executed,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the accused and 'they' are the lying pair.

phrases.english: and the second is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם נִמְצֵאת אַחַת מֵהֶן זוֹמֶמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'two testimonies' ruling to a case of הזמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two separate testimonies, if one is found זוממת, the accused and that set are executed, and the other set is exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the witnesses themselves must give the warning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules there is no execution unless the two witnesses themselves warned the sinner, learning it from 'על פי שנים עדים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: they are never executed unless his two witnesses warn him, as it says, 'By the mouth of two witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the case above, where an outsider in the middle gave the warning, and requires the witnesses themselves to warn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'by the mouth of two witnesses' as covering the warning too. The warning must come from the mouths of the witnesses. So a warning from a separate person, like the one 'in the middle,' would not be enough for him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
They are never executed

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵי עֵדָיו מַתְרִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: unless his two witnesses are warning him,
as it is said: 'By the mouth of two witnesses.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵין נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view on who must give the warning in the case of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Execution requires that the two witnesses themselves give the warning.

steps.title: Another reading: no testimony through an interpreter
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation of 'על פי שנים עדים': the סנהדרין must hear the witnesses directly, not through a translator.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'By the mouth of two witnesses' teaches that the סנהדרין may not hear testimony from the mouth of an interpreter.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a different lesson from the same words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'by the mouth of' is stressed to mean the judges must hear the words straight from the witnesses' own mouths. A translator in between would turn it into hearing from the translator's mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: The court that judges capital cases

phrases.english: Another explanation:
'By the mouth of two witnesses':
that the Sanhedrin should not
hear from the mouth of the interpreter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reading of the same פסוק used in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין may not hear testimony through an interpreter.

steps.title: רב's source that separated testimony is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב asks where we learn that עדות מיוחדת is invalid and answers with the פסוק 'לא יומת על פי עד אחד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: From where do we know that separated testimony is invalid? As it says, 'He shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by looking for the source of the משנה's idea that witnesses who did not see each other do not join together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדות מיוחדת means each witness saw the event alone, without the other. רב points to 'by the mouth of one witness' as the source, but it is not yet clear how this פסוק teaches it. That is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Separated testimony: each witness saw the event alone

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Tuvya said that Rav said:
From where do we know about separated testimony
that it is invalid?
As it is said: 'He shall not be put to death
by the mouth of one witness.'
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6, the same פסוק as 'by the mouth of two witnesses.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְעֵדוּת מְיוּחֶדֶת שֶׁהִיא פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for the משנה's rule that witnesses who don't see each other don't join.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדות מיוחדת is invalid, learned from 'לא יומת על פי עד אחד'.

steps.title: 'One witness' can't mean literally one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'one' means. If it means literally a single witness, that is already known from the first half of the פסוק, 'two witnesses.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one' mean? If you say it means literally one witness, we already learn that from the beginning of the פסוק: 'By the mouth of two witnesses'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of 'one witness' to show that the words must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק says two witnesses are needed, it is obvious that one is not enough. So saying 'not by one witness' would add nothing if read literally. That pushes us to look for a different meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
We learn it from the first part

phrases.english: What is 'one'?
If you say literally one witness,
we learn that from the beginning:
'By the mouth of two witnesses'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֶחָד? אִילֵּימָא עֵד אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in step 5 works by first ruling out the literal reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'עד אחד' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the words repeat what 'two witnesses' already teaches, so they would add nothing.

steps.title: 'One' means one here and one there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'one' means 'one, one': two witnesses each seeing separately, which counts as two single witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is 'one'? 'One, one': one witness here and one witness there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the new meaning of 'one witness': two separated witnesses are like two lone single witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though there are two people, if they each saw alone, the תורה treats each as 'one witness' by himself. So the פסוק is teaching that עדות מיוחדת is invalid, which is exactly רב's point.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One, one': each witness alone, separate from the other

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses who saw separately are treated as 'one witness' and 'one witness', so they cannot join. This is the source of the rule against עדות מיוחדת.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'one'?
One, one.
phrases.notes: He means one witness in one place and the other witness somewhere else, each seeing alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אֶחָד? אֶחָד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem of step 6 by giving a non-literal meaning to 'one'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'One' means separated witnesses, each counted alone, so their testimony does not combine.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: two windows, can't see each other
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the same פסוק that two witnesses at two windows who cannot see each other do not join.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: 'He shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness' comes to include two who see him, one from this window and one from that window, and they do not see each other: they do not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same words, 'one witness,' for the same lesson that רב taught. It applies them to the window case from the משנה. Witnesses who cannot see each other do not combine into a valid pair.

keyTerms.meaning: Also so: a source that supports what was just said
To include (a case within the rule)
Join together into one valid testimony

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:
'He shall not be put to death by the mouth of one witness':
to include two who see him,
one from this window
and one from that window,
and they do not see each other,
that they do not join.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's reading from steps 5 to 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that 'עד אחד' refers to separated witnesses, making עדות מיוחדת invalid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the same פסוק for witnesses at two windows who cannot see each other.

steps.title: Even one after another at the same window doesn't join
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that even two witnesses who watched through the same window, but one after the other, do not join.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but even if they saw one after the other through one window, they do not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes a step further and widens the rule to a case where the witnesses were in the same spot but at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think being at the same window makes them one group. But since they did not watch at the same time, each one still saw alone. So this is still עדות מיוחדת, and they do not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even: introduces a bigger case

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses must see the event together. Being separated by place (two windows) or by time (one after the other) makes them עדות מיוחדת, and they do not join.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
even one after the other
in one window,
they do not join.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה בְּחַלּוֹן אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's rule from separation by place to separation by time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses who saw one after the other, even from the same window, do not join.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need the 'one after the other' case?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if two windows don't join even when each witness saw the whole act, it is obvious that witnesses who each saw only half don't join.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Think about it. Two witnesses at two windows each saw the entire act, and you still say they don't join. So when they watched one after the other, and each one saw only half the act, do we really need to be told they don't join?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the ברייתא from Step 9. He says its second case looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-windows case each witness saw everything, which is the stronger case, and still they don't join. Watching one after the other is weaker, since each saw only part of the act. If the stronger case fails, the weaker case should fail without being told, so why does the ברייתא bother to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now', meaning 'think about it'. It opens a 'how much more so' argument
They join together to count as one pair of witnesses
'Is it necessary?' Used when something seems too obvious to say

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Now, if one witness is at this window
and one witness is at that window,
where this one sees the entire act,
and that one sees the entire act,
you say they do not join;
then one after the other,
phrases.notes: This is the second case of the ברייתא from Step 9: same window, but at different times.

phrases.english: where this one sees half the act
and that one sees half the act,
is it necessary to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא, וּמָה אֶחָד מֵחַלּוֹן זֶה וְאֶחָד מֵחַלּוֹן זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא's second case in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's case of witnesses who watched one after the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'how much more so' argument: if the stronger case (each saw everything) doesn't join, the weaker case (each saw half) obviously doesn't either.

steps.title: The case is needed for forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the 'one after the other' case is needed for someone who has relations with an ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It was only needed for the case of a man who has forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the ברייתא's second case is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With forbidden relations the act goes on over time, and even the very beginning is already enough to make a person liable. So each witness, even watching at a different moment, really saw a complete sin. You might have thought that makes them join, so the ברייתא has to teach that they still don't.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was only needed for...' Names the exact case that makes a teaching necessary
A man who has relations with a forbidden relative

phrases.english: He said to him: It was only needed
for one who has relations with a forbidden relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the teaching to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In forbidden relations each witness saw a complete sin, so we might think they join
steps.terutzMaskana: Even then, witnesses who watched one after the other do not join

steps.title: Seeing the person who warns connects the witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that witnesses at separate windows do join if they see the מתרה, or if the מתרה sees them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the witnesses could see the person giving the warning, or the person giving the warning could see them, they join together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new rule: separate witnesses can still join through the person who gives the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses who can't see each other normally don't join. But if each one can see the מתרה, or he can see both of them, he works like a link between them, and they count as one pair.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who warns the sinner before the act. A warning is needed before a בית דין can punish

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a way that 'separate' witnesses can still count together, which narrows the rule against עדות מיוחדת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If they could see the one who warns,
or the one who warns sees them, they join.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם הָיוּ רוֹאִין אֶת הַמַּתְרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a way for the window-witnesses of Step 8 to join
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses join if they see the מתרה or he sees them

steps.title: The warning can come from anyone
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a valid warning can come even from the victim himself, or from an unknown source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The warner the חכמים spoke about can be anyone. It works even if the victim warns the attacker himself, and even if the warning came from a שד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains who counts as a מתרה. Almost anyone does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning does not need to come from a third witness. Even the victim's own words count, and even a voice from an unknown source, called 'a שד'. What matters is that the sinner was warned.

keyTerms.meaning: From his own mouth, meaning the victim himself
A demon. Here it means a warning whose source is unknown

phrases.english: Rava said:
The warner that they spoke of,
even from his own mouth,
phrases.notes: He means the victim himself warned the attacker.

phrases.english: and even from the mouth of a demon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְרֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the מתרה mentioned in Step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any warning counts, even from the victim or from an unknown source

steps.title: רב נחמן: separate witnesses work in money cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the פסוק as limited to capital cases, so עדות מיוחדת is valid in דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Separate testimony is valid in money cases. The פסוק says 'He shall not die by one witness'. So only in death-penalty cases is it invalid, but in money cases it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן takes the same פסוק from Step 5 and points out that it only talks about death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'he shall not die', so its rule against 'one, one' witnesses applies only to דיני נפשות. In money cases, two witnesses who saw things separately still count.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate testimony, where each witness saw the event without the other

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not arguing with Steps 5–7. He agrees separate witnesses don't count for the death penalty. He only adds that they do count in money cases.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Separate testimony is valid in money cases,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא יוּמַת עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד״ –
phrases.english: as it is written: 'He shall not die by one witness':
it is in death-penalty cases that it is not valid,
but in money cases, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵדוּת מְיוּחֶדֶת כְּשֵׁירָה בְּדִינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the source from Steps 5–7 to capital cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדות מיוחדת is valid in דיני ממונות

steps.title: רב זוטרא: then it should save in capital cases
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא argues that if separate testimony has any force, it should at least work to save the accused, but our משנה says both he and the זוממין are executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא challenged this: If so, in capital cases separate testimony should at least save the accused! Why then did we learn in the משנה, 'he and they are executed'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זוטרא attacks רב נחמן's view using the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If separate testimony counts as real testimony, then in capital cases the two window-groups should count as one testimony when that helps save someone. Then if one group turns out to be זוממין, the whole testimony would fall and the accused would be saved. But the משנה says the accused and the זוממין are both killed, which treats the groups as fully separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it, an attack on a statement
'But now, if so...' Introduces an unwanted result of an idea
'He and they are killed.' The accused and the עדים זוממין are both executed

phrases.english: Rav Zutra challenged it:
But if so, in death-penalty cases it should save!
phrases.notes: He means: if one group is shown to be זוממין, the whole joined testimony should fall and save the accused.

phrases.english: Why did we learn: 'He and they are executed'?
phrases.notes: This is from our משנה: two groups at two windows, and one group was found to be זוממין.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב זוּטְרָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that עדות מיוחדת has legal force
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it has force, it should at least work to save in capital cases. The משנה's 'he and they are executed' shows that it does not.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב זוטרא's challenge against רב נחמן is difficult and leaves it unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by admitting it has no answer to רב זוטרא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the question remains strong against רב נחמן, but it is not a full rejection like תיובתא. His view is left with an unresolved difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult.' The question is left unanswered, but this is not a total rejection

steps.whatToRemember: Separate witnesses (עדות מיוחדת) don't join in capital cases. They can join through a מתרה, and the warning can come from anyone. רב נחמן says such testimony is valid in money cases, but רב זוטרא's challenge from the משנה is left as a קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits Step 15's challenge has no answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's view stays with an unanswered difficulty

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really require a warning?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: our משנה has רבי יוסי requiring התראה by the witnesses, but another משנה has רבי יוסי executing a שונא with no התראה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה said: רבי יוסי says (the killer is only executed if his two witnesses warn him). רב פפא asked אביי: Does רבי יוסי really hold this reasoning? But we learned in a משנה that רבי יוסי says: an enemy who kills is executed, because he is treated like someone who was warned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's opinion from our משנה. Then רב פפא points out that another משנה seems to have רבי יוסי saying the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יוסי is very strict and requires the witnesses themselves to give the התראה. In the other משנה, רבי יוסי lets a שונא be executed without any התראה, since his hatred shows he acted on purpose. One person cannot hold both positions, so רב פפא sees a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: An enemy, here someone who hated the person he killed
Like someone already cautioned and warned

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, where רבי יוסי says the two witnesses themselves must warn the killer.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַאי סְבָרָא?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei really hold this reasoning?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yosei says:
An enemy (who kills) is executed,
because he is like one who was cautioned and warned.
phrases.notes: His hatred already shows he killed on purpose, so he is treated as if he had been warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַאי סְבָרָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה, after the unanswered challenge to רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's requirement in our משנה that the witnesses must give the התראה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה has רבי יוסי executing a שונא without any התראה, which contradicts a strict התראה requirement.

steps.title: That statement belongs to a different רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה about the שונא is really the view of רבי יוסי בר יהודה, not the רבי יוסי of our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That teaching is the view of רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's contradiction by saying the two statements come from two different sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'רבי יוסי' in the משנה about the שונא is really רבי יוסי בר יהודה. The רבי יוסי of our משנה is someone else, so there is no contradiction. The next step brings a ברייתא to show that רבי יוסי בר יהודה really holds this kind of view.

keyTerms.meaning: That one, here meaning that teaching

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא – רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא.
phrases.english: That one is the view of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא – רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different author: the two statements belong to two different sages
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements come from the same רבי יוסי, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שונא ruling is רבי יוסי בר יהודה's view; our משנה's רבי יוסי consistently requires התראה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי בר יהודה does not always need a warning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that a חבר needs no התראה, because התראה only exists to tell apart שוגג from מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: A תורה scholar does not need a warning, because a warning was only given to tell the difference between someone who sins by accident and someone who sins on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי's answer, showing that רבי יוסי בר יהודה really holds that התראה is not always needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי בר יהודה, התראה is only a tool to prove the person acted on purpose. A חבר knows the law, and a שונא's hatred shows his intent, so in both cases התראה is not needed. That fits the שונא ruling and supports giving it to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A תורה scholar who knows the law
A warning given before the sin
Someone who acts by accident or without knowing

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה's רבי יוסי requires התראה by the witnesses. רבי יוסי בר יהודה sees התראה only as proof of intent, so a חבר or a שונא needs none.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
A Torah scholar does not need a warning,
because a warning was given
only to tell apart one who acts by accident from one who acts on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds a view in which התראה is not always needed, which fits the שונא ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי בר יהודה about a חבר

steps.title: No testimony through an interpreter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second reading of 'על פי שנים עדים': the סנהדרין must not hear testimony through a תורגמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'At the mouth of two witnesses' teaches that the סנהדרין should not hear testimony from the mouth of an interpreter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line from the משנה to begin a new topic. This is setting up the story about רבא and the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'at the mouth of' the witnesses, so the judges must hear the testimony directly from the witnesses themselves. Hearing it through a translator would mean hearing it from someone else's mouth.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "At the mouth of two witnesses" –
that the Sanhedrin should not
hear from the mouth of the interpreter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין may not hear testimony through an interpreter.

steps.title: רבא uses an interpreter for foreign speakers
steps.stepSummary: Some foreign-language speakers came before רבא, and he placed a תורגמן between himself and them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people who spoke a foreign language came before רבא, and רבא set up an interpreter between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבא using an interpreter. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first this seems to go directly against the משנה we just quoted. The story is told so the גמרא can ask how רבא was allowed to do this.

keyTerms.meaning: People who speak a foreign language

phrases.english: Those foreign-language speakers
who came before Rava,
Rava set up an interpreter between them.
phrases.notes: He means between רבא and the people standing before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ לָעוֹזֵי דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that seems to conflict with the rule just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא used an interpreter when foreign speakers came before him.

steps.title: How could רבא use an interpreter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's conduct from the משנה that says a סנהדרין may not hear testimony through a תורגמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? But we learned that the סנהדרין should not hear from the mouth of an interpreter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבא could use an interpreter when the משנה forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sets the story directly against the משנה from step 20. If רבא heard their words through the interpreter, he was doing exactly what the משנה says not to do.

phrases.english: And how did he do this?
But didn't we learn: that the Sanhedrin should not
hear from the mouth of the interpreter!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי עֲבִיד הָכִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 21 using the משנה in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids a סנהדרין from hearing testimony through an interpreter, yet רבא used one.

steps.title: רבא understood them but could not answer them
steps.stepSummary: רבא understood the foreign language himself; he only used the interpreter to speak back to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא understood what they were saying, but he did not know how to answer them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא heard the testimony directly, since he understood their language. The interpreter only helped him reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids the court from hearing the testimony through someone else. רבא heard their words himself, so the rule was kept. The interpreter was used only for רבא's questions and replies, which the משנה does not forbid.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule against a תורגמן is about hearing the testimony. A judge who understands the witnesses may use an interpreter just to speak back to them.

phrases.english: Rava did know
what they were saying,
it was only answering back that he did not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא מִידָּע הֲוָה יָדַע מָה דַּהֲווֹ אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the interpreter was used only for replies, not for hearing testimony
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא heard the testimony through the interpreter, which goes against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא heard the testimony directly and only used the interpreter to reply, so the משנה's rule was kept.
